                    ### Question
                    A 27-year-old woman goes to the genetic counseling clinic after having a child with Down syndrome. In the child, a trisomy 21 with translocation 21/21 inherited from the mother is identified. What would be the risk of recurrence of Down syndrome in the future children of this woman?

                    ### Options
                    opa. The risk of recurrence will be 10-15%, as in the rest of translocations.
opb. 100% of viable fetuses will be born with Down syndrome.
opc. The risk of recurrence will be very low (12%).
opd. The risk of recurrence will be 50%.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The mother has a child with Down syndrome due to a translocation 21/21, which indicates a genetic predisposition to this condition. In cases of Robertsonian translocations involving chromosome 21, the risk of recurrence for future pregnancies is significantly higher than in the general population. Specifically, the recurrence risk for a mother with a translocation 21/21 is approximately 50%. This aligns with the consensus that maternal translocations can lead to a substantial risk of having additional children with Down syndrome. Therefore, the most accurate assessment of the risk of recurrence for this woman is 50%.
